# Main Results: 6-Item Prior-Belief Index

## Average effects of the articles

```{r pooled_tables, results = "asis"}
for (v in c("Q119", "Q122", "Q123")) {
  emit_tbl(tbl_pooled(v), paste0("Pooled effects on ", out_short(v),
                                 ". Columns 1--2: additive; columns 3--4: article $\\times$ observer"))
}
```

```{r pooled_figs, results = "asis"}
res_main <- res_all |> filter(moderator == "main")
for (v in c("Q119", "Q122")) {
  emit_fig(plot_overall(res_main, v, SPEC_SETS$main, by_obs = FALSE),
           paste0("Article effects on ", out_short(v), ", all citizens"), w = 12, h = 3.8)
  emit_fig(plot_overall(res_main, v, SPEC_SETS$main, by_obs = TRUE),
           paste0("Article effects on ", out_short(v), ", by observation status"), w = 12, h = 5.5)
}
p_all_fc <- est_row(cn = CN_FC, g = "All", l = LV_ALL)
p_all_rc <- est_row(cn = CN_RC, g = "All", l = LV_ALL)
p_all_rf <- est_row(cn = CN_RF, g = "All", l = LV_ALL)
p_dif_rc <- est_row(cn = CN_RC, g = "All", l = LV_DIFF)
```

*Interpretation.* Pooling all citizens, the fraud article changes perceived fraud by `r fe(p_all_fc)` relative to control, and the allegation-plus-rebuttal article by `r fe(p_all_rc)`. The rebuttal-versus-fraud difference is `r fe(p_all_rf)`. Without the prior-belief split, the observer--non-observer difference in the allegation-plus-rebuttal effect is `r fe(p_dif_rc)`. The next sections ask whether this pooled comparison hides heterogeneity by prior beliefs.

## Raw means by observation status and prior belief

```{r cibars_main, results = "asis"}
for (v in c("Q119", "Q122")) {
  emit_fig(cibar_by_obs(v), paste0("Mean ", out_short(v),
           " by article, observers vs. non-observers. Bars: 95\\% CIs; brackets: Welch $t$-test $p$-values"),
           w = 10, h = 5)
  emit_fig(cibar_by_belief(v, "main"), paste0("Mean ", out_short(v),
           " by article, observation status, and prior belief (6-item index)"), w = 10, h = 8)
}
```

*Interpretation.* The key panel is the top row of the Q119 figure (high prior belief). Among high-belief observers, the allegation-plus-rebuttal article changes perceived fraud by `r fe(k_obs_hi)` relative to control; among high-belief non-observers, by `r fe(k_non_hi)`. The bottom row shows the same comparison for low-belief citizens. The bars show raw means, so these differences equal the contrasts in the tables below (without covariates).

## Focal contrast: allegation plus rebuttal vs. control

```{r maintext_tables, results = "asis"}
for (v in c("Q119", "Q122")) {
  emit_tbl(make_main_text_tex(res_all, v, "main"),
           paste0("Effect of the allegation-plus-rebuttal article relative to control on ", out_short(v),
                  ", by observation status and prior belief (6-item index)"))
}
k122 <- est_row(var = "Q122")
```

*Interpretation.* This is the candidate main-text table. For Q119, the observer--non-observer difference among high-belief citizens, $\Delta_{2C}(1)$, is `r fe_ci(k_focal)`. Among low-belief citizens, $\Delta_{2C}(0)$ is `r fe(k_low)`. For trust in election administration (Q122), $\Delta_{2C}(1)$ is `r fe(k122)`; a positive value would mean observers' trust rises relative to non-observers'.

## All contrasts by observation status and prior belief

```{r si_main, results = "asis"}
for (v in c("Q119", "Q122")) {
  emit_tbl(make_si_tex(res_all |> filter(moderator == "main"), v, SPEC_SETS$main, MOD_NOTE[["main"]]),
           paste0("All article contrasts for ", out_short(v), ": no covariates and demographic controls (6-item index)"), fit = TRUE)
  emit_fig(plot_contrasts(res_all |> filter(moderator == "main"), v, SPEC_SETS$main),
           paste0("Article contrasts for ", out_short(v), " by observation status and prior belief (6-item index)"),
           w = 12, h = 7)
}
k_holm <- k_focal$p.holm
```

*Interpretation.* Panel C tests whether the observer--non-observer gap differs by prior belief. For allegation plus rebuttal versus control, $\Omega_{2C}$ is `r fe(k_omega)`. The Holm-adjusted $p$-value for $\Delta_{2C}(1)$ in Panel B is `r sprintf("%.3f", k_holm)`. For rebuttal versus fraud (question b), $\Delta_{21}(1)$ is `r fe(k_rf)` and $\Omega_{21}$ is `r fe(k_rf_om)`. In the figure, the middle column corresponds to question (a) and the right column to question (b).

## Three-way interaction regression

```{r threeway_main, results = "asis"}
emit_tbl(tbl_threeway("main"),
         "Three-way interaction model (6-item index). Reference: control article, non-observers, low prior belief",
         small = TRUE, fit = TRUE)
```

*Interpretation.* This table reports the regression in the Empirical Strategy. The (Fraud + Rebuttal) $\times$ Observer $\times$ High prior belief coefficient is $\delta_2 = \Omega_{2C}$ and matches Panel C of the contrast table (`r num(k_omega$estimate, 3)` without covariates). The Fraud $\times$ Observer $\times$ High coefficient is $\delta_1$.

## Adjusting for continuous prior beliefs

```{r si_appx, results = "asis"}
for (v in c("Q119", "Q122")) {
  emit_tbl(make_si_tex(res_all |> filter(moderator == "main"), v, SPEC_SETS$appx, MOD_NOTE[["main"]]),
           paste0("All article contrasts for ", out_short(v), ": adding the continuous 6-item index"), fit = TRUE)
  emit_fig(plot_contrasts(res_all |> filter(moderator == "main"), v, SPEC_SETS$appx),
           paste0("Article contrasts for ", out_short(v), ", adding the continuous 6-item index"),
           w = 12, h = 7)
  emit_fig(plot_overall(res_all |> filter(moderator == "main"), v, SPEC_SETS$appx, by_obs = TRUE),
           paste0("Article effects on ", out_short(v), " by observation status, adding the continuous 6-item index"),
           w = 12, h = 5.5)
}
```

*Interpretation.* The median split groups respondents with different prior beliefs. Within a group, the arms can still differ somewhat in the continuous index. Adding the continuous index moves $\Delta_{2C}(1)$ from `r num(k_focal$estimate)` (no covariates) and `r num(k_focal_d$estimate)` (demographic controls) to `r fe(k_focal_p)` (additive) and `r fe(k_focal_l)` (Lin). This is the "weakens after adjustment" caveat in the key takeaway.

## Balance of prior beliefs within groups

```{r balance_prior_main, results = "asis"}
emit_tbl(make_balance_prior_tex("main"),
         "Continuous 6-item index by observation status, prior-belief group, and article")
sd_obs_hi <- prior_std_diff("main", "Obs", "Hi")
sd_non_hi <- prior_std_diff("main", "Non", "Hi")
```

*Interpretation.* Within the high-belief group, the standardized difference in the continuous index between the allegation-plus-rebuttal and control arms is `r num(sd_obs_hi)` among observers and `r num(sd_non_hi)` among non-observers. Differences of this kind are one reason the adjusted estimates in Section 3.6 can differ from the unadjusted ones.

## Continuous moderator (interflex)

```{r interflex_main, results = "asis"}
for (bn in c("median", "terciles")) {
  for (sp in names(IF_SPECS)) {
    for (v in c("Q119", "Q122")) {
      safely(emit_fig(plot_if(v, sp, bn, "main"),
                      paste0("Conditional effects on ", out_short(v), " over the continuous 6-item index (",
                             tolower(sp), "; ", bn, " bins)"), w = 12, h = 8),
             paste("interflex figure", v, sp, bn))
    }
  }
}
for (bn in c("median", "terciles")) {
  safely(emit_tbl(wald_tex("main", bn),
                  paste0("Wald tests of the linear interaction model against the binning model (6-item index; ",
                         bn, " bins)"), small = TRUE, fit = TRUE),
         "Wald table")
}
if_hi <- if_bin |> filter(mod == "main", outcome == "Q119", spec == "No covariates",
                          bins == "median", contrast == CN_RC, x > med_6)
if_hi_obs <- if_hi |> filter(obs == "Obs")
if_hi_non <- if_hi |> filter(obs == "Non")
```

```{r interflex_diag, results = "asis"}
emit_tbl(knitr::kable(compare_tbl |> mutate(obs = ifelse(obs == "Obs", "Observers", "Non-observers")),
                      format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "",
                      col.names = c("Outcome", "Group", "Prior belief", "Comparison",
                                    "Diff. in means", "Section 7", "Local linear", "interflex")),
         "Check: interflex binned estimates (median bins, no covariates) vs. differences in means", small = TRUE, fit = TRUE)
```

*Interpretation.* The binned estimates come from a local linear fit within each bin, evaluated at the bin median, so they need not equal the median-split differences in means; the check table shows how large the gap is. Above the median, the interflex estimate for allegation plus rebuttal versus control is `r if (nrow(if_hi_obs) == 1) num(if_hi_obs$estimate) else "n/a"` among observers and `r if (nrow(if_hi_non) == 1) num(if_hi_non$estimate) else "n/a"` among non-observers (Q119, no covariates). The histograms at the bottom of each panel show whether both arms have support across the index. Wald $p$-values below 0.05 suggest the linear interaction model is too restrictive.

## Subgroup regression tables by prior belief

```{r bybelief_tables, results = "asis"}
for (v in c("Q119", "Q122")) {
  emit_tbl(tbl_by_belief(v, "main"),
           paste0("Effects on ", out_short(v), " within prior-belief groups (6-item index)"), small = TRUE, fit = TRUE)
}
```

*Interpretation.* These tables estimate the pooled specification separately for high- and low-belief citizens. The (Fraud + Rebuttal) $\times$ Observer coefficient in column 3 of Panel A equals $\Delta_{2C}(1)$, and in Panel B it equals $\Delta_{2C}(0)$.

## Robustness: party identification and perceived fairness

```{r other_mods, results = "asis"}
for (v in c("Q119", "Q122")) {
  for (am in names(ALT_MODS)) {
    emit_fig(plot_contrasts(res_other |> filter(moderator == am), v, SPEC_SETS$main,
                            ALT_MODS[[am]]$lo, ALT_MODS[[am]]$hi),
             paste0("Article contrasts for ", out_short(v), ", split by ",
                    if (am == "ppp") "PPP identification" else "perceived fairness of the 2024 election"),
             w = 12, h = 7)
  }
  emit_fig(plot_contrasts(res_other |> filter(moderator == "prior_std_main"), v, names(STD_SPECS)),
           paste0("Article contrasts for ", out_short(v), " by prior belief (6-item index), standardized to party and fairness composition"),
           w = 12, h = 7)
}
o_ppp  <- est_row(mod = "ppp",  res = res_other)
o_fair <- est_row(mod = "fair", res = res_other)
o_std  <- est_row(mod = "prior_std_main", spec = "Standardized: party + fairness", res = res_other)
```

*Interpretation.* Is the prior-belief pattern just party or fairness perceptions under another name? Splitting by PPP identification instead, the observer--non-observer difference in the allegation-plus-rebuttal effect among PPP identifiers/leaners is `r fe(o_ppp)`. Splitting by perceived fairness, it is `r fe(o_fair)` among those with high perceived fairness. When the prior-belief contrasts are standardized to the same party and fairness composition, $\Delta_{2C}(1)$ is `r fe(o_std)`.

## Robustness: number of items in the index

```{r robust_items, results = "asis"}
for (v in c("Q119", "Q122")) {
  emit_fig(plot_robust_items(v),
           paste0("Focal estimates for ", out_short(v), " across prior-belief measures built from 1 to 6 items"),
           w = 12, h = 5.5)
}
rob_rng <- rob |> filter(outcome == "Q119", spec == "No covariates", estimand == ROB_EST[2]) |>
  summarise(lo = min(estimate), hi = max(estimate))
```

*Interpretation.* Across measures built from 1 to 6 items, $\Delta_{2C}(1)$ for Q119 (no covariates) ranges from `r num(rob_rng$lo)` to `r num(rob_rng$hi)`. Sections 4 and 5 show the full set of results for the 3-item and 1-item measures.
